title: Circuit synthesis by CEGIS
description: Counterexample-guided inductive synthesis: two-input gates (and, or, nand) wired into a circuit that computes the majority of its inputs. The synthesiser only sees input/output examples; the verifier holds the specification and returns an input where the circuit is wrong, with the wanted output. Each such input is grounded in the synthesiser from refine(k) (Shape 3), so the synthesiser simulates the circuit on it. Solutions: every circuit of g gates that computes the majority, as wirings (counts checked by brute force over all circuits).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% A circuit of g two-input gates over the inputs 1 .. m. Nodes 1 .. m are the inputs, nodes
% m + 1 .. m + g the gates; the last gate is the output. A gate reads two earlier nodes.
inp(1..m).
gate(m+1..m+g).
node(1..m+g).
kind(and; or; nand).
outnode(m+g).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The synthesiser guesses a circuit: each gate's kind and its two inputs (A < B, both
% earlier). Every gate but the output feeds a later gate.
1 { op(G,O) : kind(O) } 1 :- gate(G).
1 { arg(G,A,B) : node(A), node(B), A < B, B < G } 1 :- gate(G).
used(A) :- arg(_,A,_).
used(B) :- arg(_,_,B).
:- gate(G), not outnode(G), not used(G).
#show op/2.
#show arg/3.

#program refine(k).
% The k-th counterexample input: cex(k,inval(I,V)) gives input I the value V, and
% goal(k,want(V)) the value the specification wants. Simulate the circuit on this input
% (w(k,N): node N is 1) and require the wanted output.
w(k,I) :- cex(k,inval(I,1)).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,and), w(k,A), w(k,B).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), w(k,A).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), w(k,B).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not w(k,A).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not w(k,B).
:- outnode(N), w(k,N), goal(k,want(0)).
:- outnode(N), not w(k,N), goal(k,want(1)).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
glue(op(G,O)) :- gate(G), kind(O).
glue(arg(G,A,B)) :- gate(G), node(A), node(B), A < B, B < G.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% The verifier: an input on which the circuit and the specification disagree.
{ x(I) } :- inp(I).
v(I) :- x(I).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,and), v(A), v(B).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), v(A).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), v(B).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not v(A).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not v(B).
out :- outnode(N), v(N).
% The specification (only the verifier knows it): the majority of the inputs.
ones(N) :- N = #count { I : x(I) }.
spec :- ones(N), 2 * N > m.
:- out, spec.
:- not out, not spec.
% The counterexample as data for the synthesiser: the input and the wanted output.
inval(I,1) :- x(I).
inval(I,0) :- inp(I), not x(I).
want(1) :- spec.
want(0) :- not spec.
#show inval/2.
#show want/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# CEGIS (counterexample-guided inductive synthesis, Solar-Lezama et al.): the synthesiser
# proposes a circuit that is right on the inputs seen so far; the verifier looks for an
# input where it is wrong. Each such input is grounded in the synthesiser (Shape 3), which
# then has to simulate the circuit on it. The specification itself stays in the verifier.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(inval/2), goal = X.atoms(want/1))
        count inputs
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

instances.facts: % Majority of 3 inputs with 4 gates: 27 circuits (brute force).
% Majority of 3 inputs with 5 gates: 789 circuits (brute force), still 7 counterexample inputs.
% Majority of 3 inputs with 3 gates: none (brute force).
% At least 3 of 4 inputs with 5 gates: none (brute force); 12 counterexample inputs to show it.
% Both of 2 inputs (and) with 3 gates: 23 circuits.
% Majority of 2 inputs (both must be 1) with 1 gate: the and gate.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Shape 4: search, collect the counterexample inputs, ground them in batches of four.
pending = []
repeat:
    search A:
        on candidate M:
            X = C.solve(assume G(M))
            if X:
                pending.push(X)
                reject M with G.block(M)
                if pending.size >= 4: restart
    grounded = pending.size
    for X in pending:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(inval/2), goal = X.atoms(want/1))
        count inputs
    pending.clear()
until A.exhausted and grounded == 0

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to two counterexample inputs per circuit, each grounded in the synthesiser.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    XS = C.models(assume G(M), limit 2)
    for X in XS:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(inval/2), goal = X.atoms(want/1))
        count inputs
    if XS.size == 0:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

library.summary: CEGIS: circuits of and/or/nand gates that compute the majority, synthesised from the counterexample inputs a verifier returns; each input is grounded as a simulation in the synthesiser (3 inputs, 4 gates, 27 solutions).
